app.title: 🎛️ ACE-Step V1.5 Playground💡
app.subtitle: Pushing the Boundaries of Open-Source Music Generation

dataset.title: 📊 Dataset Explorer
dataset.dataset_info:
### Selection

Choose the HuggingFace or local dataset to explore.

- **Expected format**: ACE-Step-compatible dataset (audio + captions)
- **Examples**: `my-dataset`, `user/dataset-name`, `./data/local_ds`

Use this explorer to check the content before training.
dataset.search_type_info:
### Search mode

Method for accessing a dataset sample.

- **Keys**: search by exact key/name (e.g. `track_001`)
- **Index**: direct access by numerical position (e.g. `42`)

Use **Index** to browse sequentially, **Keys** to target a specific sample.
dataset.search_value_placeholder: Enter keys or index (leave empty for random)
dataset.search_value_info:
### Search value

Input based on the chosen mode.

- **Keys**: **exact** match required (case sensitive)
- **Index**: integer between `0` and `dataset_size - 1`

**Example**: for a 500-item dataset, valid indices are `0` to `499`.
dataset.use_src_info:
### Use source audio

Check to reuse the **source audio** from the dataset as input for the current task.

- **Enabled**: the original audio is injected (edit, extend, remix)
- **Disabled**: generation from scratch with no audio reference
- **Tip**: enable for editing or continuation tasks

service.title: 🔧 Service Configuration
service.checkpoint_info:
Loads the **DiT model weights** that drive audio generation. Choice impacts speed, features, and quality.

### Variants

- **Turbo**: 4–8 diffusion steps, very fast, great for drafts and iteration.
- **Base**: slower but unlocks full feature set — guidance scale, extract/lego modes, finer control.

### When to use

- Pick `turbo` for quick generation and exploration.
- Pick `base` when you need maximum control or advanced modes.
service.model_path_info:
Points to the **directory containing the model config and architecture files**. Auto-detected from your checkpoint selection.

### When to change

- Only override if you have a **custom model setup** (fork, local fine-tune, non-standard layout).
- Leave as-is in normal use — the wrong path will break initialization.
service.device_info:
Selects the **hardware backend** used to run the models.

### Options

- `auto`: picks the best available device (recommended).
- `cuda`: NVIDIA GPU — fastest path on supported hardware.
- `mps`: Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4).
- `xpu`: Intel GPU.
- `cpu`: very slow, use only as a last resort.
service.lm_model_path_info:
Selects the **language model** that powers LLM-assisted features.

### Features it enables

- **Think mode** (chain-of-thought planning before DiT generation).
- **CoT metadata** auto-fill (BPM, key, time signature, language).
- **Caption enhancement** and **semantic code generation**.

### Trade-off

- Larger LMs produce better results but consume more **VRAM**.
- Required for Think mode — cannot be skipped if you rely on it.
service.backend_info:
Inference **engine** used by the 5Hz LM.

### Options

- **vLLM**: significantly faster inference. Recommended for NVIDIA GPUs with **≥8 GB VRAM**.
- **PyTorch (`pt`)**: slower but works on all hardware (CPU, MPS, XPU).

### When to use `pt`

- vLLM fails to install.
- Running on non-NVIDIA hardware (Apple Silicon, Intel, CPU).
service.init_llm_info:
Loads the **5Hz Language Model** (a small LLM specialized in music understanding) into memory at startup. This unlocks several AI-assisted features.

### Features unlocked

**Think mode** (`thinking=True`)

The LLM plans the audio codes via chain-of-thought reasoning before the DiT generates the waveform. Improves musical coherence and lyric/audio alignment.

**AI Draft** (Create Sample)

Generate metadata (BPM, key, time signature, language) and lyrics from a free-text description in Simple mode.

**CoT Metas**

The LLM auto-fills missing BPM, key, time signature and language fields from your caption.

**CoT Language**

Auto-detects the vocal language from your lyrics.

**CaptionRewrite**

The LLM rewrites short captions into richer, more model-friendly prompts before generation.

**Auto Score**

Calculates a quality score for each generated sample to compare batch outputs.

**Enhance Caption / Enhance Lyrics**

Buttons available in Custom mode to polish your inputs via the LLM.

### VRAM cost

- `0.6B` model: ~1.2 GB
- `1.7B` model: ~3.4 GB
- `4B` model: ~8 GB

On **Apple Silicon** (MPS), the model uses unified memory.

### When to disable

Disable this option to save memory if you only generate from a fully-formed Custom prompt with manual BPM, key and lyrics, and don't need any LLM-assisted feature. Disabling forces all CoT, Think and AI Draft features to be unavailable.
service.lm_unavailable_vram: ⚠️ LM not available for this GPU tier (VRAM too low)
service.flash_attention_info_enabled:
Enables **Flash Attention** for the DiT inference path.

### Benefits

- **~20–30% speedup** on DiT inference.
- Lower memory usage.
- **No quality difference** — purely a performance optimization.

### Requirements

- The `flash_attn` package must be installed.
- Recommended to keep enabled when available.
service.flash_attention_info_disabled:
**Flash Attention is not available** — the `flash_attn` package is not installed.

### How to enable

- Install with: `pip install flash-attn`
- Provides **~20–30% speedup** on DiT inference.
- **No quality change** — purely a performance optimization.
service.offload_cpu_info:
Moves inactive models to **system RAM** to free GPU VRAM for the active model.

### Trade-off

- Adds a small delay (**~1–3 s**) when switching between models.
- Frees significant VRAM during generation.

### When to use

- **Essential** on GPUs with **<16 GB VRAM**.
- **Negligible impact** on GPUs with **>24 GB VRAM** — can be left off.
service.offload_dit_cpu_info:
Also offloads the **DiT model** to CPU, on top of the base offload.

### Trade-off

- Saves more VRAM but adds **extra swap time** each generation.
- Requires **Offload to CPU** to be enabled first.

### When to use

- Very low VRAM GPUs (**<10 GB**).
- Skip it otherwise — the latency cost isn't worth it on mid/high-end GPUs.
service.compile_model_info:
Optimizes the model using **PyTorch compilation** for faster inference.

### Trade-off

- **First generation** takes longer (compilation overhead).
- **Subsequent generations** run **~10–20% faster**.

### Notes

- **Required** if you want to use INT8 quantization.
- Recommended to keep enabled in most setups.
service.quantization_info:
Applies **INT8 quantization** to the model weights (32-bit → 8-bit).

### Benefits

- Cuts VRAM usage by **~50%** with minimal quality loss.
- **Essential** for GPUs with **<16 GB VRAM**.

### Requirements & limits

- Requires **Compile Model** to be enabled.
- **Incompatible with LoRA adapters** — disable quantization if you need LoRA.
service.mlx_dit_info_enabled:
Runs the **DiT diffusion model** using Apple's native **MLX framework** instead of PyTorch MPS.

### Benefits

- Significantly faster on **M1/M2/M3/M4 Macs**.
- Uses unified memory efficiently.

### When to use

- Recommended for all Apple Silicon users — enable it when available.
service.mlx_dit_info_disabled:
**MLX is not available** in this environment.

### Requirements

- **macOS** running on **Apple Silicon** (M1/M2/M3/M4).
- The `mlx` package must be installed.

### How to enable

- Install with: `pip install mlx`
- Then restart the service to switch the DiT path to MLX.
service.status_info:
Shows the **current state** of the service.

### What it displays

- Loading progress while models initialize.
- Errors if initialization fails.

### How to use

- Click **Initialize Service** to load the models.
- Watch this field for feedback during startup.
service.language_info:
Selects the **interface language** used across the Gradio UI.

### Notes

- Affects labels, tooltips, and messages.
- Does not affect generated lyrics or model behavior.
service.tier_info:
Overrides the **auto-detected GPU capability tier**.

### What the tier controls

- Defaults for **CPU offload**, **quantization**, and **backend** selection.
- Tuned to match your available **VRAM** budget.

### When to override

- Auto-detection picks the wrong tier for your setup.
- You want to **force specific optimization settings** (e.g. disable offload on a large GPU).
- Leave on `Auto` unless you have a clear reason to change it.

generation.task_type_info:
### Task type
Selects the **generation mode** used internally by the model.

- **Automatically set** when you pick a mode in the UI
- Controls which inputs are required (source audio, time range, stems, etc.)
- Advanced users can override it manually to access specific pipelines
generation.instruction_info:
### Automatic instruction

This field is **generated automatically** based on the selected task type (text2music, edit, extend, etc.).

- **Read-only** in most cases
- **Role**: passes the current task context to the model
- **Modification**: leave as-is unless you have an advanced prompt engineering need
generation.track_name_info:
### Track name
Selects which **single stem** to target.

- **Used by**: `Lego` and `Extract` modes
- **Examples**: `vocals`, `drums`, `bass`, `guitar`, `piano`, `other`
- **Lego**: the chosen stem is replaced by the AI
- **Extract**: the chosen stem is isolated from the source audio
generation.track_classes_info:
### Track classes
Selects **multiple stems** to generate at once.

- **Used by**: `Complete` mode only
- **Examples**: `drums`, `bass`, `guitar`, `piano`, `other`
- Pick every track that is **missing** from your source audio
- The AI generates all selected stems together so they fit musically
generation.lm_codes_info:
### LM codes (hints)

Paste **latent codes** to guide text2music generation with a precise sonic prior.

- **Usage**: stylistic continuity or pattern reproduction
- **Format**: serialized codes from a previous generation
- **Optional**: leave empty for free generation
- **Tip**: useful for iterating on the same sonic identity
generation.lm_codes_sample_info:
### Codes for sample `{n}`

Latent codes specific to **sample #{n}** in the current session.

- **Role**: per-variation hint, allows diversifying outputs while keeping a common base
- **Optional**: leave empty to let the model explore
- **Tip**: copy codes from a successful output to refine that variation
generation.mode_info:
Choose how you want to generate music. Each mode has a different workflow and level of control.

### Simple

**Best for**: quick ideas, brainstorming, users new to ACE-Step

**You provide**: a plain-language description

**AI generates**: caption, lyrics, BPM, key, structure, and audio

### Custom

**Best for**: users who know exactly what they want

**You provide**: caption, lyrics, BPM, key, duration, and all parameters

**AI generates**: audio matching your exact specifications

### Remix

**Best for**: restyling an existing song with new lyrics or genre

**You provide**: source audio + new caption/lyrics

**AI generates**: a restyled version using the original as structural guide

**Note**: adjust `Remix Strength` — high stays faithful, low reinterprets loosely

### Repaint

**Best for**: fixing a bad section without regenerating the whole track

**You provide**: source audio + a time range (`start`/`end` in seconds)

**AI generates**: new audio only inside that range, rest stays untouched

### Extract

**Best for**: making instrumentals, acapellas, or isolated stems

**You provide**: source audio + track to isolate (vocals, drums, bass, etc.)

**AI generates**: the chosen stem via AI separation

**Note**: **Base model only** — not available in turbo

### Lego

**Best for**: swapping one instrument while keeping the rest of the mix

**You provide**: source audio + which stem to replace + new caption/lyrics

**AI generates**: a replacement track fitted to the original context

**Note**: **Base model only** — not available in turbo

### Complete

**Best for**: turning a partial mix into a full arrangement

**You provide**: source audio with missing tracks + which classes to generate

**AI generates**: the missing stems (drums, bass, etc.) to complete the mix

**Note**: **Base model only** — not available in turbo

### Model compatibility

**Turbo model**: supports `Simple`, `Custom`, `Remix`, `Repaint`

**Base model**: supports all 7 modes including `Extract`, `Lego`, `Complete`
generation.mode_info_simple:
### Simple mode
- **Best for**: quick ideas, brainstorming, or when you're unsure what settings to use
- **You provide**: a plain-language description of the music you want
- **AI generates**: caption, lyrics, BPM, key, structure, and final audio

Switch to **Custom** if you want full manual control over every parameter.
generation.mode_info_custom:
### Custom mode
- **Best for**: users who know exactly what they want
- **You provide**: caption, lyrics, BPM, key, duration, and all generation parameters
- **AI generates**: audio strictly matching your specifications

Switch to **Simple** if you'd rather describe an idea and let the AI fill in the technical details.
generation.mode_info_remix:
### Remix mode
- **Best for**: restyling an existing track with a new genre, mood, or lyrics
- **You provide**: source audio + your own caption and lyrics
- **AI generates**: a restyled version using the original as a structural guide

### Remix Strength
- **High**: faithful cover, closely follows the original
- **Low**: loose reinterpretation, more creative freedom
generation.mode_info_repaint:
### Repaint mode
- **Best for**: fixing a bad section or replacing a specific part without regenerating the whole track
- **You provide**: source audio + a time range (`start`/`end` in seconds)
- **AI generates**: new audio inside that range only

**Outside the selected range, the original audio stays untouched.**
generation.mode_info_extract:
### Extract mode
- **Best for**: creating instrumentals, acapellas, or isolated stems for remixing
- **You provide**: source audio + the track to isolate (vocals, drums, bass, etc.)
- **AI generates**: the chosen stem via AI source separation

**Note**: this mode is **Base model only** — not available with the turbo model.
generation.mode_info_lego:
### Lego mode
- **Best for**: swapping one instrument while keeping the rest of the mix intact
- **You provide**: multi-track source audio + the stem to replace + new caption/lyrics
- **AI generates**: a replacement track fitted to the surrounding context

**Note**: this mode is **Base model only** — not available with the turbo model.
generation.mode_info_complete:
### Complete mode
- **Best for**: turning a partial mix into a full arrangement
- **You provide**: source audio with missing tracks (e.g. just vocals and guitar) + which classes to generate
- **AI generates**: the missing stems (drums, bass, etc.) to create a full mix

**Note**: this mode is **Base model only** — not available with the turbo model.
generation.simple_query_placeholder: Describe the music you want to create, e.g., 'a soft Bengali love song for a quiet evening'. Leave empty for a random sample.
generation.simple_query_info:
### Natural description

Describe in plain language the music you want to generate. The model interprets genre, mood, instruments, and structure.

- **Examples**: `upbeat synthwave with driving bass and retro leads`, `melancholic acoustic ballad, fingerpicked guitar, female vocals`
- **Tip**: be specific about genre, tempo, and key instruments
- **Language**: English recommended for best results
generation.simple_vocal_language_info:
### Lyrics language

Select the preferred language(s) for sung vocals. Influences pronunciation and phrasing.

- **`unknown`**: let the model choose automatically
- **Multi-language**: possible for bilingual tracks
- **Tip**: align this choice with the actual language of the `lyrics` field
generation.caption_placeholder: A peaceful acoustic guitar melody with soft vocals.
generation.caption_info:
### Stylistic caption

Precisely describe the sonic identity of the track. The richer the caption, the more faithful the generation.

- **Genre**: `synthpop`, `lo-fi hip-hop`, `orchestral cinematic`
- **Instruments**: `electric guitar riff`, `analog synth pad`, `808 drums`
- **Mood**: `uplifting`, `melancholic`, `energetic`
- **Tempo feel**: `120 BPM driving`, `slow 70 BPM groove`
- **Vocals**: `male tenor`, `female soulful`, `whispered`

**Example**: `upbeat pop with guitar riff, punchy drums, female vocals, 128 BPM, summer vibe`
generation.lyrics_placeholder: [Verse 1]\nUnder the starry night\nI feel so alive.
generation.lyrics_info:
### Structured lyrics

Write the lyrics with **structure tags** to guide the composition. Tags are mandatory for a coherent result.

- **Supported tags**: `[Verse]`, `[Chorus]`, `[Bridge]`, `[Instrumental]`, `[Intro]`, `[Outro]`
- **Tip**: alternate `[Verse]` and `[Chorus]` for a classic structure

**Example**:

`[Verse]
Walking down the empty street
[Chorus]
We are the fire, we are the night
[Bridge]
Hold on, don't let go
[Instrumental]`
generation.dit_preset_info:
### Quality presets

- **Fast**: `8 steps` — turbo models
- **Balanced**: `15 steps` — speed/quality trade-off
- **Quality**: `30 steps` — polished rendering
- **Custom**: manual setting

**Tip**: choose based on the loaded model (turbo vs base).
generation.vocal_language_info:
Language of the generated vocals. Align it with the language of your lyrics for a better result.

### Special values

- **`unknown`**: let the model decide (ideal for **instrumental** or **multilingual**)
- **`instrumental`**: force the complete absence of vocals

### Tip

An explicit language improves **pronunciation** and **prosody**.
generation.bpm_info:
Song tempo, in beats per minute.

### Typical ranges by genre

- **Slow ballad**: `60–80` BPM
- **Pop / Rock**: `100–130` BPM
- **Dance / EDM**: `120–140` BPM
- **Fast punk / Metal**: `160–200` BPM

### Auto mode

Leave empty or check **`Auto`** to let the model choose based on your caption.
generation.keyscale_placeholder: e.g. C Major, A Minor, F# Minor
generation.keyscale_info:
Musical key of the song.

### Examples

- **Major**: `C Major`, `G Major`, `D Major` — **bright / joyful** sound
- **Minor**: `Am`, `F# Minor`, `Em` — **dark / melancholic** sound

### Auto mode

Leave empty or check **`Auto`** to let the model decide based on the caption and lyrics.
generation.timesig_info:
Number of beats per measure (time signature).

### Common values

- **`4`** → 4/4, most **pop / rock / electronic**
- **`3`** → 3/4, **waltz** feel
- **`6`** → 6/8, **compound and flowing** feel
- **`2`** → 2/4, **march** feel

### Auto mode

Use **`N/A`** or **`Auto`** to let the model decide.
generation.duration_info:
Length of the generated audio, in seconds.

### Impact

- Longer durations require **more VRAM** and **more** generation **time**
- **`-1`**: the model decides based on the lyrics and structure

### Auto mode

Check **`Auto`** for an automatic duration tailored to the content.
generation.batch_size_info:
Number of variations generated in parallel.

### Trade-off

- **Higher**: more options to compare, but increased **VRAM** and **time**
- **Lower**: fast iterations, fewer choices

### Recommendation

Generate **`2–4`** variations to compare and pick the best take.
generation.inference_steps_info:
### Number of denoising passes

More steps = better quality but slower.

- **Turbo**: `4–8` (default `8`, diminishing returns beyond)
- **SFT**: `30–100` (default `50`)
- **Base / unknown**: default `32`

**Note**: doubling the steps roughly doubles the generation time.
generation.guidance_scale_info:
### Prompt fidelity (CFG)

Controls how closely the output follows your description.

- **High** (`10–15`): very faithful but sometimes harsh/distorted sound
- **Low** (`1–5`): more natural/creative but may drift
- **Default**: `7.0`

**Base only**: no effect on turbo models.
generation.seed_info:
### Generation seed

Same seed + same settings = same output (reproducible).

- **Fixed integer**: identical result on every run
- **CSV list** (e.g. `42,123,456`): one seed per batch sample
- **`-1`**: random

**Usage**: fix a seed to reproduce a specific result.
generation.random_seed_info:
### Automatic random seed

- **Enabled**: new seed on every generation, unique results
- **Disabled**: the fixed seed above is used

**Tip**: disable to reproduce a specific output.
generation.audio_format_info:
### Available formats

- **FLAC** — lossless, large files, perfect quality
- **WAV 32-bit** — studio quality, largest files
- **MP3** — compact files, slight quality loss
- **Opus / AAC** — efficient lossy compression

### When to use

- **Production / archiving**: `FLAC` or `WAV`
- **Sharing / streaming**: `MP3`, `Opus`, or `AAC`
generation.use_adg_info:
### ADG guidance (experimental)

Alternative guidance method to standard CFG.

- Better prompt adherence with **fewer artifacts**
- Useful if you get distortion at **high guidance scales**
- **Experimental**: does not always improve results

**When to try**: harsh/saturated sound with classic CFG.
generation.shift_info:
### Noise schedule timing

Controls the distribution of denoising effort.

- **High** (`3–5`): effort concentrated on the **first steps** (better structure)
- **Low** (`1–2`): effort distributed (finer details)
- **Default**: `3.0`

**Base only**: ignored by turbo models.
generation.infer_method_info:
### Inference method

- **ODE (Euler)**: deterministic and faster. Same seed → same result. **Recommended** in most cases.
- **SDE (Stochastic)**: injects randomness during diffusion. More varied/creative results but **less predictable**.

**When to use SDE**: if ODE sounds too "safe" or uniform.
generation.sampler_mode_info:
### Numerical solver

- **Euler**: first order, fast (**default**)
- **Heun**: second-order predictor-corrector, evaluates the model **2x per step** for more precision

**Heun benefit**: cleaner audio, particularly in **turbo 8-step** mode.

**Cost**: about `2x` the diffusion time.
generation.velocity_norm_threshold_info:
### Velocity norm clamp

Limits velocity predictions relative to input norms at each diffusion step.

- **`0`**: disabled
- **`1.5–3.0`**: reduces artifacts
- **Starting point**: `2.0`

**Usage**: prevents aberrant predictions that cause audio artifacts.
generation.velocity_ema_factor_info:
### Velocity EMA smoothing

Exponential moving average between the current and previous prediction to smooth the denoising trajectory.

- **`0`**: disabled
- **`0.05–0.2`**: effective range
- **Starting point**: `0.1`

**Benefit**: cleaner output, more stable trajectory.
generation.custom_timesteps_info:
### Manual denoising schedule (advanced)

Explicitly define the timestep sequence as CSV from `1.0` down to `0.0`.

**Example**:

`0.97,0.76,0.615,0.5,0.395,0.28,0.18,0.085,0`

- **Override**: replaces **Inference Steps** and **Shift**
- **Empty**: automatic scheduling

**Warning**: only use if you know what you are doing.
generation.cfg_interval_start_info:
### CFG interval start

When CFG guidance begins during denoising.

- **`0.0`**: from the beginning (default)
- **`1.0`**: never
- **Low values**: longer guidance → stronger prompt adherence
- **High values**: skips the first steps → **reduces artifacts**

**Base only**: no effect on turbo.
generation.cfg_interval_end_info:
### CFG interval end

When CFG guidance stops during denoising.

- **`1.0`**: until the end (default)
- **`0.0`**: immediately
- **Low values**: early stop → free final steps, **less harshness**
- **High values**: extended guidance → stronger prompt control

**Base only**: no effect on turbo.
generation.lm_temperature_info:
Controls the creativity of the 5Hz LM by adjusting sampling randomness.

### Values

- **0.0–0.5**: safe and conventional musical choices
- **0.6–0.9**: recommended balance (default `0.85`)
- **1.0–1.5**: more creative and surprising, but risky
- **1.5+**: chaotic, may produce nonsense

### When to use

- **Lower** for classic styles or predictable results
- **Raise** to explore unexpected variations
- Start at `0.85` then adjust based on results

### Notes

Interacts with **Top-K** and **Top-P**: a high temperature amplifies the effect of these filters.
generation.lm_cfg_scale_info:
How strongly the LM follows the prompt rather than generating freely.

### Values

- **1.0**: no guidance, the LM ignores the prompt influence
- **1.5–2.0**: moderate guidance, good balance
- **2.5–3.0**: strong guidance, very faithful but reduced variety
- **5.0–7.0**: maximum control, may degrade quality or introduce artifacts
- **>7.0**: experimental

### When to use

- **Raise** if the prompt is poorly respected
- **Lower** if the music feels rigid or artificial

### Notes

- Requires a **negative prompt** to work (set automatically if empty)
- Active only when the **5Hz LM** is enabled
generation.lm_top_k_info:
Limits the LM's choices to the `K` most probable tokens at each step.

### Values

- **0**: disabled, no filtering (recommended default)
- **10–30**: focused and predictable output
- **50–100**: more diversity

### When to use

- **Enable** to constrain diversity to a precise style
- **Leave at 0** if you already use **Top-P**

### Notes

Works alongside **Top-P**: both filters can be active simultaneously and stack.
generation.lm_top_p_info:
Keeps only the tokens whose cumulative probability reaches `P` (nucleus sampling).

### Values

- **0.5–0.8**: very focused
- **0.9–0.95**: recommended default, trims unlikely outliers
- **1.0**: disabled, all tokens considered

### When to use

- Prefer over **Top-K** as it is more adaptive to context
- **Lower** for a more conservative output

### Notes

Can be combined with **Top-K** and **Temperature** for fine sampling control.
generation.lm_negative_prompt_placeholder: Enter negative prompt for CFG (default: NO USER INPUT)
generation.lm_negative_prompt_info:
Tells the LM what to **avoid** during generation.

### Values

- **Empty**: default behavior (auto-filled if `CFG Scale > 1.0`)
- **Example**: `low quality, noise, distorted` to steer away from poor outputs

### When to use

- To explicitly push away undesired characteristics
- Combine with a high **CFG Scale** to reinforce the effect

### Notes

- **Only effective** when **LM CFG Scale > 1.0**
- The LM moves away from this prompt and closer to your actual caption
generation.cot_metas_info:
Enables the LM's *chain-of-thought* reasoning over musical metadata (**BPM**, **key**, **structure**) before generation.

### Values

- **Enabled** (recommended): more coherent results, cost `+2–5s` per generation
- **Disabled**: directly uses your manual metadata

### When to use

- **Enable** if you let the model infer BPM/key/structure
- **Disable** if you have already filled in all metadata manually

### Notes

The LM "thinks" about musical parameters before sampling, improving structural coherence.
generation.cot_language_info:
Enables automatic vocal language detection during *chain-of-thought* reasoning.

### Values

- **Enabled**: the LM infers the language from context
- **Disabled**: uses the explicitly set language

### When to use

- **Enable** when the language is ambiguous or set to `unknown`
- **Disable** if you have explicitly set the vocal language

### Notes

Avoids conflicts between a manually set language and the one detected by the LM.
generation.constrained_debug_info:
Shows detailed logs of the filtering and constraints applied to LM output tokens.

### Values

- **Enabled**: verbose logs for each constraint step
- **Disabled**: normal usage (recommended)

### When to use

- **Developers only**, when debugging token generation
- To inspect why certain tokens are rejected

### Notes

Affects log readability and may slightly slow execution. Leave disabled in production.
generation.auto_score_info:
### Description

Automatically computes a **quality score** (0–1) for each generated audio via `perplexity`. Higher score = better perceptual quality.

### Usage

- Compare multiple generations within the same batch
- Automatically identify the best take
- Filter out failed samples

### Cost

- Adds **a few seconds** of computation per sample
- Negligible on small batches, noticeable on massive generations

### Interactions

- Works with `Score Sensitivity` to adjust score dispersion
- Enables score display in results for comparison
generation.auto_lrc_info:
### Description

Automatically generates **synchronized lyrics** in `LRC` format (timestamps) for each produced audio.

### Usage

- Synchronized **karaoke** display
- Subtitle export for video
- Verification of lyrics/audio alignment

### Cost

- Adds processing time per sample
- Impact proportional to audio duration

### Interactions

- Requires input lyrics (otherwise automatic transcription)
- Applies independently to each batch sample
generation.lm_batch_chunk_info:
### Description

Number of samples processed simultaneously by the **Language Model** during batch generation.

### Values

- **Default**: `8`
- **Recommended range**: `1–16` depending on available VRAM
- `1–4`: GPU with **<12 GB VRAM**
- `8+`: high-end GPU (24 GB+)

### Recommendations

- Increase for **faster** batch generation
- Reduce on **out-of-memory** (OOM) errors
- Test progressively to find the maximum stable value

### Interactions

- Direct impact on LM VRAM usage
- Does not affect quality, only speed and memory
generation.codes_strength_info:
### Description

Fraction of **DiT denoising** steps that use the semantic codes produced by the LM as musical guidance.

### Values

**Default**: `1.0` (good starting point)

- `0.7–1.0`: the output **faithfully** follows the LM's musical plan
- `0.1–0.4`: the DiT has more **creative freedom**
- `0.0`: LM codes **completely ignored**

### Recommendations

- Keep high to respect the structure and intent of the prompt
- Lower for unexpected creative variations
- Set to `0` to test the DiT in standalone mode

### Interactions

- Complementary to `Remix Strength` and `Cover Strength`
- Directly influences the coherence between text prompt and final audio
generation.cover_strength_info:
### Description

Fraction of denoising steps that **reference the structure** of the source audio to guide generation.

### Values

- **High**: output close to the **original**
- **Low**: freer **creative reinterpretation**

### Recommendations

- Increase for covers faithful to the original structure
- Reduce for exploratory remixes
- Adjust in small increments (`0.1`) to fine-tune

### Interactions

- Tune jointly with `Cover Strength (Melody Retention)` for fine remix control
- Cumulative effect with `Remix Strength` on overall fidelity
generation.remix_strength_info:
### Description

Controls the **closeness** between the generated remix and the source audio (structure + melody).

### Values

**Default**: `0.5` (balanced starting point)

- `0.7–1.0`: very close to the original, **subtle stylistic changes**
- `0.1–0.4`: free interpretation, **major creative liberties**

### Recommendations

**Raise** for faithful covers (same structure, new style)

**Lower** for wild remixes and radical transformations

- Iterate in steps of `0.1` to calibrate

### Interactions

- Combines with `Cover Noise Strength` for melodic retention
- Interacts with `Codes Strength` for the source/prompt balance
generation.cover_noise_strength_info:
### Description

Controls the **amount of original melody preserved** during the remix.

### Values

- `0.0`: **no melodic retention** (pure style transfer from caption)
- `0.1–0.25`: **recommended range** with the `SFT` model (restores melody while allowing style changes)
- `1.0`: **maximum melodic retention**

### Recommendations

- Start in `0.1–0.25` for a balanced remix
- Lower toward `0` for full style transfer
- If high values **resist** style changes, enrich or rephrase the caption

### Interactions

- Works in tandem with `Remix Strength`
- Depends on the loaded model (optimal with the `SFT` variant)
- Direct tension with the text prompt: the higher the retention, the less influence the caption has
generation.enable_normalization_info:
### Role

Adjusts the final volume to a constant peak level.

### Benefits

- Prevents **clipping** (distortion from a signal that is too loud)
- Ensures **consistent loudness** across generations
- Predictable results from one render to the next

### Recommendation

Leave **enabled** for consistent outputs.
generation.normalization_db_info:
### Reference values

- **`-1.0 dB`** — industry standard, safety margin (**recommended**)
- **`-0.1 dB`** — maximum loudness before clipping
- **`-3.0 dB` and below** — quieter, reserved for later mixing/mastering

### Principle

The lower the value, the more **headroom** remains for later processing.
generation.fade_in_duration_info:
### Role

Gradually increases the volume from silence at the start of the track.

### Typical values

- **`0s`** — no fade, full-volume start
- **`1–3s`** — subtle intro
- **`5–10s`** — slow, dramatic build-up

### Usage

Useful for avoiding **abrupt starts**.
generation.fade_out_duration_info:
### Role

Gradually decreases the volume toward silence at the end of the track.

### Typical values

- **`0s`** — no fade, may cut off abruptly
- **`2–5s`** — soft and natural ending

### Usage

Avoids **hard cut-offs** at the end of generation.
generation.latent_shift_info:
### Advanced parameter

Shifts the internal latent representation before audio decoding.

### Values

- **`0`** — no shift (**default**)
- **`-0.04`** and other small negative values — worth trying in case of clipping or distortion

### Warning

Only adjust **if you hear audio artifacts**. Inappropriate modification can degrade quality.
generation.latent_rescale_info:
### Advanced parameter

Scales the internal latent representation before decoding.

### Values

- **`1.0`** — no rescale (**default**)
- **`< 1.0`** (e.g. `0.91`) — reduces residual clipping and distortion

### Warning

Use **only if normalization is not enough** to eliminate audible artifacts.
generation.score_sensitivity_info:
### Description

Controls the **mapping function** between raw perplexity and the normalized `0–1` score.

### Values

**Default**: `1.0`

**Low values** (e.g. `0.5`): **more spread-out** scores, easy to distinguish good/bad

**High values**: scores **clustered** in a narrow range

### Recommendations

- Lower if all scores **look too similar**
- Raise if gaps are **exaggerated** and unrepresentative
- Adjust after several generations to calibrate for your usage

### Interactions

- Requires `Auto Score` enabled to have an effect
- Does not affect audio quality, only the **interpretation** of displayed scores
generation.lora_path_info:
### LoRA adapter

Path to the folder of your **trained LoRA adapter**.

### Workflow

- Train a LoRA in the `Training` tab
- Click **Export** to generate the adapter folder
- Paste the path here (or download a community LoRA)

### Trigger tag

Some LoRAs require an **activation tag** in the prompt/caption (e.g. `mystyle`, `v2-vocal`). Check the LoRA documentation.

### Warning

Incompatible with **INT8** quantization — disable INT8 if you want to use a LoRA.
generation.use_lora_info:
### LoRA activation

Enables or disables the loaded LoRA adapter during generation.

- **ON**: the trained style of the LoRA is applied
- **OFF**: generation with the base model (useful for A/B comparison)

### Trigger tag

If your LoRA was trained with an **activation tag**, remember to include it in the caption when enabled.

### Warning

LoRA loading is **incompatible with INT8 quantization**. Use `bfloat16` or `float16` if you enable this option.
generation.lora_scale_info:
### LoRA style intensity

Controls the **strength of application** of the trained style.

### Typical values

- `0.0` — no effect (equivalent to base model)
- `0.5` — blended, subtle style
- `1.0` — full LoRA effect *(recommended starting point)*
- `> 1.0` — over-amplification, risk of artifacts

### Recommendation

Start at **`1.0`** then reduce gradually if the style is too strong or overrides the prompt. If the effect is too weak, first check that the LoRA's **trigger tag** is present in the caption before going above `1.0`.
generation.parallel_thinking_info:
Processes LM reasoning in parallel for all samples in a batch instead of one by one.

### Values

- **Enabled**: faster, uses more **VRAM**
- **Disabled**: sequential, reduced memory footprint

### When to use

- **Enable** when `batch size > 1` and VRAM is sufficient
- **Disable** on **out-of-memory** errors with large batches

### Notes

Only has an effect if multiple samples are generated simultaneously.
generation.caption_rewrite_info:
Lets the LM enrich and expand your caption before generation.

### Values

- **Enabled**: your brief description is rewritten into a detailed and *model-friendly* prompt
- **Disabled**: your caption is used as-is

### When to use

- **Enable** if you write short captions and want the LM to fill in musical details
- **Disable** to keep strict control over the prompt

### Notes

Useful for turning a vague idea into a structured description (genre, instruments, mood).
generation.mp3_bitrate_info:
### MP3 encoding bitrate

Controls the **quality / file size** trade-off.

### Typical values

- **`128 kbps`** — acceptable quality, light files (basic streaming)
- **`192 kbps`** — good general trade-off
- **`256 kbps`** — high quality, subtle difference from lossless
- **`320 kbps`** — **MP3 maximum**, recommended for polished delivery

### Tip

For web sharing, `192` or `256 kbps` is sufficient. For MP3 archiving, prefer `320 kbps`.
generation.mp3_sample_rate_info:
### MP3 sample rate

Sampling frequency of the encoded file.

### Supported values

- **`44.1 kHz`** — CD and consumer music standard
- **`48 kHz`** — video and broadcast standard

### Tip

Choose `44.1 kHz` for **pure music** usage, `48 kHz` if the audio will be integrated into **video**.
generation.repainting_start_info:
### Repainting Start

Start timestamp (in **seconds**) of the zone to regenerate inside the source audio.

- Range: `0` to end-of-audio
- Audio **before** this point stays untouched
- Combined with the **Repaint Strength** slider:
  - `0.0` Conservative — subtle edits, keeps source
  - `0.5` Balanced — blend of source + regeneration
  - `1.0` Aggressive — full regeneration of the zone
generation.repainting_end_info:
### Repainting End

End timestamp (in **seconds**) of the repaint zone.

- Use `-1` to repaint **until the end of file**
- Must be greater than *Repainting Start*
- Audio **after** this point stays untouched
- Boundary smoothing is handled by `repaint_latent_crossfade_frames` and `repaint_wav_crossfade_sec` to avoid clicks at the splice
generation.stem_start_info:
### Stem Start

Start timestamp (in **seconds**) of the working zone for **Extract** (stem isolation) and **Lego** (stem replacement) modes.

- Range: `0` to end-of-audio
- Audio outside `[start, end]` is left as-is
- Use tight bounds to target a specific phrase, verse or chorus
generation.stem_end_info:
### Stem End

End timestamp (in **seconds**) of the Extract/Lego working zone.

- Use `-1` to process **until the end of file**
- Must be greater than *Stem Start*
- In **Lego** mode, only the selected stem inside this window is replaced; other stems and the outside region are preserved
generation.instrumental_info:
### Instrumental

Forces a **vocal-free** generation.

- **Checked** — no vocals are generated, the model produces a pure instrumental track (lyrics field is ignored)
- **Unchecked** — vocals are generated following the `lyrics` field and the selected `vocal language`

Useful for backing tracks, karaoke beds, or when the caption already implies an instrumental style.
generation.autogen_label_info:
### AutoGen

Auto-chains generation batches in the **background** while you listen to the current one.

- Queues the next batch as soon as the current finishes
- Lets you review results without idle GPU time
- Stop anytime from the queue panel
- Ideal for **exploration sessions** where you iterate on a caption/lyrics
generation.think_label_info:
### Think Mode (5Hz LM)

Enables **chain-of-thought** reasoning on the 5Hz LM over audio codes before the diffusion pass.

- Requires the **LM to be initialized** (loaded in memory)
- Improves **audio/lyrics coherence**, phrasing and musical structure
- Slightly increases generation time
- Recommended for complex lyrics, narrative songs, or tight rhythmic alignment
generation.reference_audio_info:
### Reference Audio *(optional)*

Upload an audio file used as **style guidance** in **Custom** mode.

- Supported: `wav`, `mp3`, `flac`
- The model extracts timbre, mood and production hints from the reference
- Does **not** copy melody or lyrics — only style
- Leave empty to rely solely on the caption
generation.source_audio_info:
### Source Audio *(required)*

Input audio file consumed by modes that edit existing material:

- **Remix** — restyle with a new caption/lyrics
- **Repaint** — regenerate a time range
- **Extract** — isolate a stem
- **Lego** — replace a stem
- **Complete** — fill in missing tracks

Supported: `wav`, `mp3`, `flac`. Ignored in *Simple* and *Custom* modes.
generation.bpm_auto_label_info:
### BPM Auto

Lets the **LM decide the BPM** from the caption.

- **Checked** — manual BPM slider is **overridden**, BPM is inferred from the prompt semantics (`fast punk` → ~180, `lo-fi chill` → ~70)
- **Unchecked** — the manual BPM value is enforced

Useful when the style implies a tempo you don't want to specify by hand.
generation.key_auto_label_info:
### Key Auto

Lets the **LM decide the musical key** from the caption.

- **Checked** — manual Key selector is **overridden**, the model picks a key matching mood/genre
- **Unchecked** — the manual Key value is enforced

Helpful for matching conventional genre keys (e.g. sad ballad → minor).
generation.timesig_auto_label_info:
### TimeSig Auto

Lets the **LM decide the time signature** from the caption.

- **Checked** — manual TimeSig selector is **overridden** (e.g. `waltz` → `3/4`, `metal` → `4/4`, `prog` → `7/8`)
- **Unchecked** — the manual Time Signature is enforced
generation.vocal_lang_auto_label_info:
### Language Auto

Lets the **LM decide the vocal language** from the caption and lyrics.

- **Checked** — manual Vocal Language selector is **overridden**, inferred from lyrics script and caption cues
- **Unchecked** — the manual language is enforced

Falls back to `unknown` for multilingual or ambiguous inputs.
generation.duration_auto_label_info:
### Duration Auto

Lets the **LM decide the track duration** from the caption.

- **Checked** — manual Duration slider is **overridden**, length is inferred from structure hints (`intro + 2 verses + chorus` → longer, `jingle` → short)
- **Unchecked** — the manual Duration value is enforced
generation.lora_lokr_warning: > ⚠️ **LoKr adapters cannot be stacked.** Loading a LoKr adapter replaces any active PEFT LoRA. Standard LoRA adapters can be stacked with up to several adapters at once.
generation.lora_adapter_name_info: Unique name used to identify the adapter in the table. Leave empty to derive a default from the path basename.
generation.user_mode_info: Beginner hides advanced DiT/LM/Automation settings to keep the UI clean. Switch to Expert when you need fine-grained control over sampling, velocity tweaks, CFG intervals, and debug flags.

training.load_dataset_info:
### Loading

Reloads a dataset already saved in JSON format.

- Avoids **re-scanning** and re-labeling audio files
- Allows resuming manual caption editing
- Useful after an interruption or to adjust tags

**Typical workflow**: `scan` → `label` → `save` → `load` (resume).
training.scan_info:
### Directory scan

Recursively browses the folder and detects supported audio files.

- **Formats**: `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.flac`, `.ogg`, `.opus`
- Creates an entry per file found, ready for labeling

**Tip**: organize your audio files in a dedicated folder before scanning to avoid duplicates.
training.step2_instruction:
Click the button below to use AI to automatically generate metadata for all audio files:
- **Caption**: Music style, genre, mood description
- **BPM**: Beats per minute
- **Key**: Music key (e.g. C Major, Am)
- **Time Signature**: 4/4, 3/4 etc.
training.step5_intro:
**Preprocessing converts your dataset into pre-computed tensors for fast training.**

You can:
- Use the dataset from steps 1-4 above, **OR**
- Load an existing dataset JSON file (if you have one saved)
training.step5_details:
This step will:
- Encode audio to VAE latents
- Encode captions and lyrics to text embeddings
- Run condition encoders
- Save all tensors to `.pt` files

⚠️ **This requires loading models and may take a few minutes.**
training.train_tensor_selection_desc:
Select the directory containing preprocessed tensor files (`.pt` files).
These are created using the 'Preprocess' button in the 'Dataset Builder' tab.
training.all_instrumental_info:
### Instrumental tracks

Marks **all** samples as instrumental (no vocals).

- Automatically adds the `instrumental` tag to captions
- Avoids the `vocal` prompt during generation

Enable only if **100%** of the dataset is vocal-free (orchestral music, lofi beats, ambient).
training.custom_tag_info:
### Trigger tag

Unique keyword used to activate your LoRA style during inference.

- Must be **unique** and unambiguous
- **Good examples**: `myname-style-v1`, `cyberpunk-lofi-xyz`
- **Bad examples**: `cool`, `music`, `style` (too generic)

This tag will be injected into each caption according to the chosen position.
training.tag_position_info:
### Tag position

Location of the trigger tag in the final caption.

- **Prefix**: `myname-style-v1, rock, guitar, 120bpm`
- **Suffix**: `rock, guitar, 120bpm, myname-style-v1`

**Prefix** generally gives more weight to the trigger during LoRA training.
training.genre_ratio_info:
### Caption/Genre ratio

Weighting between descriptive caption and genre tags during training.

- **0%**: uses only the full **caption**
- **100%**: uses only the **genres**
- **50%**: balanced mix

**Note**: an override set on an individual sample **overrides** this global ratio.
training.skip_metas_info:
### Skip metadata

Skips the automatic generation of BPM, Key, and TimeSignature.

- **Captions** and **genres** are still generated by the LM
- Speeds up the process if musical metadata is not critical

Useful for styles where tempo/key vary (ambient, experimental, sound design).
training.only_unlabeled_info:
### Unlabeled samples

Labels only entries that have no caption.

- **Use case**: resume an interrupted or failed labeling run
- Preserves existing captions (manual or auto)
- Avoids wasting LM compute

**Workflow**: `load` partial dataset → check → `label` → `save`.
training.select_sample_info:
### Sample selection

Choose an individual sample to **preview** and **edit**.

- Listen to the audio
- Manually edit the caption
- Override the genre ratio for this sample only

Use after scan or load to verify/correct generated labels.
training.caption: Caption
training.prompt_override_info:
### Local ratio override

Overrides the Caption/Genre ratio **only** for this sample.

- Takes precedence over the global slider
- Useful when a track needs specific handling

**Example**: global dataset at `50%`, but an orchestral track forced to `0%` (caption only) for richer descriptive details.
training.save_path_info:
### Save path

Destination JSON file for the labeled dataset.

- **Absolute**: `/Users/name/datasets/my_lora.json`
- **Relative**: `./datasets/my_lora.json`
- `.json` extension recommended

This file contains captions, genres, audio paths, and metadata — reloadable via `Load Dataset`.
training.load_existing_info:
### Existing dataset path

Previously saved JSON file to reload.

- **Absolute**: `/path/to/dataset.json`
- **Relative**: `./datasets/dataset.json`
- Must follow the Dataset Builder output format

**Workflow**: lets you resume editing or move on to tensor preprocessing.
training.tensor_output_info:
### Tensors folder

Destination for preprocessed `.pt` files (VAE latents + embeddings).

- **Absolute**: `/Users/name/training/tensors/`
- **Relative**: `./tensors/lora_v1/`
- Created automatically if it does not exist

**Size**: expect several GB depending on duration and number of samples.
training.preprocessed_tensors_info:
### Preprocessed tensors folder

Directory containing the `.pt` files generated in the previous step.

- **Absolute**: `/Users/name/training/tensors/`
- **Relative**: `./tensors/lora_v1/`
- Must exactly match the `tensor_output` from preprocessing

This folder directly feeds the LoRA training **dataloader**.
training.dataset_info:
### Dataset information

Synthetic summary of the currently loaded dataset.

- Total number of samples
- Cumulative duration
- Labeling status (labeled / unlabeled)
- Source path

Check this info before launching preprocessing to avoid surprises.
training.lora_rank_info:
### LoRA capacity

Dimension of the low-rank matrices. Determines the **learning capacity** of the adaptation.

- **Typical range**: `16` to `128`
- **Beginner**: start at `32` or `64`
- **Advanced**: `128+` for complex styles

The higher the rank, the more VRAM consumed and the larger the file size.

> **Warning**: LoRA is incompatible with INT8 quantization.
training.lora_alpha_info:
### Scale factor

Controls the **effective intensity** of the LoRA adaptation applied to the model weights.

- **Common rule**: `alpha = 2 × rank`
- **Rank 32** -> alpha `64`
- **Rank 64** -> alpha `128`

An alpha equal to the rank gives a scaling of `1.0` (more conservative). A higher alpha amplifies the training effect.
training.learning_rate_info:
### Learning rate

Speed at which LoRA weights are updated at each step.

- **Default value**: `3e-4`
- **Conservative**: `1e-4` (more stable)
- **Aggressive**: `5e-4` (fast convergence, risk of overfit)

To be adjusted based on dataset size and the stability of the loss observed during training.
training.batch_size_info:
### Batch size

Number of samples processed **simultaneously** per training step.

- **Direct impact** on VRAM usage
- **Beginner**: `1` to `2`
- **Advanced**: increase as long as VRAM allows

A larger batch stabilizes gradients but requires more memory. Use `Gradient Accumulation` if VRAM is limited.
training.gradient_accumulation_info:
### Gradient accumulation

Simulates a larger batch without using more VRAM.

```
Effective Batch Size = batch_size × accumulation_steps
```

- **Example**: `batch_size=2` + `accum=4` = effective batch of `8`
- **Usage**: limited VRAM but need for more stable gradients

Slows down training proportionally to the number of accumulated steps.
training.shift_info:
### Temporal shift

Shift of the **timestep** distribution during training.

- Specific to **Turbo** / distilled models
- **Default**: typically `3.0`

Only adjust if the target model uses a scheduler with a particular shift. Leave at the default for standard models.
training.output_dir_info:
### Output directory

Folder where the trained LoRA weights will be **saved**.

- Per-epoch checkpoints included
- Final weights in `.safetensors` format

> Check available disk space before starting a long training run. Use an absolute path to avoid any ambiguity.
training.lokr_no_checkpoints_use_latest: ℹ No checkpoints found; export will use latest available weights
training.lokr_no_exportable_checkpoints: ℹ No exportable epoch checkpoints found
training.lokr_no_weights_selected_epoch: ❌ No LoKr weights found for selected epoch: {epoch}
training.lokr_no_weights_latest_checkpoint: ❌ No LoKr weights found in latest checkpoint: {checkpoint}
training.lokr_no_trained_weights_found: ❌ No trained LoKr weights found in {path}
training.lokr_tensor_selection_desc:
Select the directory containing preprocessed tensor files (`.pt` files).
These are created using the 'Preprocess' button in the 'Dataset Builder' tab.
training.lokr_linear_dim_info:
### LoKr dimension

Rank of the matrices in the **Kronecker** decomposition used by LoKr.

- **Typical range**: `8` to `64`
- **Beginner**: `16` or `32`
- **Advanced**: `64+` for complex tasks

LoKr is more parameter-efficient than LoRA at equal capacity, allowing more modest dimensions.
training.lokr_linear_alpha_info:
### LoKr alpha

Scale factor of LoKr adaptations.

- **Common rule**: `alpha ≈ dim`
- Effective scaling of `1.0` when equal
- Increase to amplify the training effect

Unlike LoRA, LoKr often uses an alpha close to the dim rather than double.
training.lokr_factor_info:
### Kronecker factor

Controls the **shape** of the Kronecker decomposition of weight matrices.

- **`-1`**: automatic detection (recommended)
- Positive values: manual control

Leave on auto unless you have a specific need for memory optimization or a constraint on the structure.
training.lokr_decompose_both_info:
### Decompose both matrices

Applies the Kronecker decomposition to **both sides** (left and right) of the target matrix.

- **Enabled**: more expressive, slightly more parameters
- **Disabled**: one-sided decomposition, lighter

Recommended for complex styles that require fine weight adaptation.
training.lokr_use_tucker_info:
### Tucker decomposition

Applies the **Tucker** decomposition on convolution layers when relevant.

- Improves expressiveness on 4D tensors
- No effect on purely linear layers

Advanced option: enable for models containing significant convolutions.
training.lokr_use_scalar_info:
### Scalar gating

Enables a **learned scalar** that dynamically modulates the intensity of LoKr weights.

- Improves training **stability**
- Negligible parameter cost

Recommended as a default option for more robust training.
training.lokr_weight_decompose_info:
### DoRA — Weight decomposition

Enables the **weight decomposition into magnitude + direction** (DoRA technique).

- **Improved quality** over standard LoKr
- More **stable** training
- Slight overhead in VRAM and time

Strongly recommended for the best results, especially on small datasets.
training.lokr_learning_rate_info:
### LR for LoKr

LoKr typically requires a **higher** learning rate than LoRA.

- **LoKr**: `~1e-3`
- **LoRA**: `~1e-4`
- Ratio of about **10×**

LoKr also converges roughly **10× faster** than LoRA thanks to its Kronecker structure. Adjust based on the dataset.
training.lokr_output_dir_info:
### LoKr output directory

Folder for **saving** the trained LoKr weights.

- Per-epoch checkpoints
- `.safetensors` format

> LoKr files are generally **smaller** than equivalent LoRA files thanks to the Kronecker decomposition. Use an absolute path to avoid any confusion.
training.lokr_checkpoint_epoch_info:
### Checkpoint to export

Choice of the **epoch checkpoint** to convert/export.

- **`Latest`**: automatic selection of the most recent
- **Specific epoch**: to test intermediate states

Useful for comparing several epochs and keeping the one offering the best quality / overfit trade-off.

help.getting_started:
## Getting Started

1. **Select a model** in the Settings accordion (e.g. `acestep-v15-turbo`)
2. **Choose a 5Hz LM** if you want Thinking mode (recommended)
3. Click **Initialize Service** and wait for the green status
4. Pick a **Generation Mode** (start with Simple)
5. Describe your music and click **Generate Music**

> **Tip:** Turbo models are fastest. Enable "Think" for smarter generation.
help.service_config:
## Service Configuration

### Quick Setup
1. Select **Main Model Path** (turbo recommended)
2. Select **5Hz LM Model Path** (auto-filtered by GPU)
3. Choose **Backend**: `vllm` (fast, NVIDIA ≥8GB) or `pt` (universal)
4. Check **Initialize 5Hz LM** for Thinking mode
5. Click **Initialize Service**

### Performance Tips
- **Flash Attention**: Faster inference (needs flash_attn)
- **CPU Offload**: Auto-enabled on GPUs <20GB
- **INT8 Quantization**: Reduces VRAM, auto-enabled <20GB
- **Compile**: Required for quantization, enabled by default

### LoRA
- Set LoRA path → Load → Enable "Use LoRA"
- ⚠️ Cannot use LoRA with INT8 quantization
help.generation_simple:
## Simple Mode Tutorial

**Best for:** Quick music creation with minimal effort.

### Steps
1. Select **Simple** in Generation Mode
2. Type a description, e.g. *"upbeat pop song with catchy guitar riff"*
3. (Optional) Check **Instrumental** for no vocals
4. (Optional) Select **Vocal Language**
5. Click **Create Sample** — AI generates caption, lyrics, metadata
6. Review and edit the generated content if needed
7. Click **Generate Music**

### Tips
- Click 🎲 for random inspiration
- The more specific your description, the better the result
- Leave BPM/Key empty to let AI decide
help.generation_custom:
## Custom Mode Tutorial

**Best for:** Full creative control over every parameter.

### Steps
1. Select **Custom** in Generation Mode
2. Write a detailed **Caption** describing style, genre, instruments, mood
3. Write **Lyrics** with structure tags: `[Verse]`, `[Chorus]`, `[Bridge]`
4. (Optional) Upload **Reference Audio** for style guidance
5. Set **BPM**, **Key**, **Duration** or leave empty for auto
6. Click **Format** to enhance with LM (optional)
7. Click **Generate Music**

### Caption Tips
- Be specific: *"dreamy shoegaze with reverb-heavy guitars and whispered vocals"*
- Include: genre, instruments, mood, tempo feel, vocal style
help.generation_remix:
## Remix Mode Tutorial

**Best for:** Creating cover versions or style transfers.

### Steps
1. Select **Remix** in Generation Mode
2. Upload **Source Audio** (the song to remix)
3. Write a **Caption** describing the target style
4. (Optional) Modify **Lyrics**
5. Adjust **Remix Strength** (0.0–1.0):
   - Higher = closer to original structure
   - Lower = more creative freedom
6. Click **Generate Music**

### Tips
- Start with strength 0.5 and adjust
- Use SFT model with Cover Strength 0.1–0.25 for melody retention
help.generation_repaint:
## Repaint Mode Tutorial

**Best for:** Fixing or regenerating specific sections of generated music while keeping the rest intact.

### Steps
1. Select **Repaint** in Generation Mode
2. Upload **Source Audio**
3. Set **Repainting Start** (seconds) and **End** (-1 for end of file)
4. Write a **Caption** for the repainted section
5. Choose a **Repaint Mode** and adjust **Repaint Strength** if needed
6. Click **Generate Music**

### Repaint Mode
Controls how the model treats non-repainted regions:

- **Conservative** (Strength = 0): Maximum source preservation. Source latents are injected at every diffusion step with long boundary crossfades. Best for seamless blending.
- **Balanced** (default): Source latents are injected for a fraction of steps controlled by the Repaint Strength slider. Good starting point.
- **Aggressive** (Strength = 1): No source injection at all — pure diffusion. Maximum creative freedom but less boundary consistency.

### Repaint Strength
Only active in **Balanced** mode. Drag to control the preserve-vs-regenerate tradeoff:
- **0** = Conservative behavior (auto-switches mode)
- **0.5** = Default — inject source during first 50% of steps
- **1** = Aggressive behavior (auto-switches mode)

### Tips
- Use "Send To Repaint" from Results to quickly load audio
- Start with Balanced (0.5) and adjust based on results
- Lower strength for better boundary consistency, higher for more creative output
help.generation_extract:
## Extract Mode (Base Model Only)

**Best for:** Stem separation — isolating instruments from a mix.

### Steps
1. Select **Extract** in Generation Mode
2. Upload **Source Audio**
3. Select **Track Name** to extract (e.g. vocals, drums, bass)
4. Click **Extract Stem**

### Available Tracks
vocals, backing_vocals, drums, bass, guitar, keyboard, percussion, strings, synth, fx, brass, woodwinds
help.generation_lego:
## Lego Mode (Base Model Only)

**Best for:** Adding new instrument tracks to existing audio.

### Steps
1. Select **Lego** in Generation Mode
2. Upload **Source Audio**
3. Select **Track Name** to add
4. Write a **Caption** describing the track
5. Click **Add Stem**

### Tips
- Great for layering: add drums to a guitar track, add bass to vocals
- The caption should describe only the new track's characteristics
help.generation_complete:
## Complete Mode (Base Model Only)

**Best for:** Auto-arranging — filling in missing instruments.

### Steps
1. Select **Complete** in Generation Mode
2. Upload **Source Audio** (partial arrangement)
3. Select multiple **Track Names** to add
4. Write a **Caption** describing the desired style
5. Click **Generate Music**
help.generation_caption:
## Writing Good Captions

### Structure
A good caption includes:
- **Genre/Style**: pop, rock, jazz, electronic, classical…
- **Instruments**: guitar, piano, synth, drums, strings…
- **Mood**: upbeat, melancholic, energetic, dreamy…
- **Vocal style**: whispered, powerful, falsetto, rap…
- **Tempo feel**: fast, slow, moderate, driving…

### Examples
- *"Energetic pop-punk with distorted guitars, fast drums, and shouted vocals"*
- *"Smooth jazz trio with walking bass, brushed drums, and mellow piano"*
- *"Ambient electronic with layered synth pads and no vocals"*

### Tips
- More detail = better results
- Use the **Format** button to let AI enhance your caption
- Check 🎲 for example captions
help.generation_lyrics:
## Writing Lyrics

### Structure Tags
Use section tags to structure your song:
```
[Verse 1]
Your verse lyrics here

[Chorus]
Your chorus lyrics here

[Verse 2]
Second verse here

[Bridge]
Bridge section

[Outro]
Ending lyrics
```

### Tips
- Keep verses 4–8 lines
- Choruses should be memorable and repetitive
- Use `[Instrumental]` or `[Interlude]` for non-vocal sections
- Check **Instrumental** checkbox for pure instrumental music
- Select **Vocal Language** to match your lyrics language
help.generation_advanced:
## Advanced Settings

### Key Parameters
- **Inference Steps**: Turbo=8 (default), Base=up to 200. More steps ≠ always better for turbo
- **Guidance Scale**: Base model only. Higher = follows prompt more strictly
- **Shift**: Timestep shift (1.0–5.0). 3.0 recommended for turbo
- **Seed**: Set a specific seed for reproducible results

### LM Parameters
- **Temperature** (0.0–2.0): Higher = more creative/random
- **CFG Scale** (1.0–3.0): Higher = follows prompt more
- **Top-K / Top-P**: Sampling strategies for diversity

### Think Mode
Enable **Think** to use 5Hz LM for smarter generation:
- Generates semantic codes and metadata
- Requires LM to be initialized
- **ParallelThinking**: Process batches in parallel (faster)
help.results:
## Results Section

### Per-Sample Controls
- **Audio Player**: Play, pause, download
- **Send To Remix/Repaint**: Use this result as source for further editing
- **Save**: Export audio + metadata as JSON
- **Score**: Calculate quality score (perplexity-based)
- **LRC**: Generate lyrics timestamps

### Batch Navigation
- Use **◀ Previous** / **Next ▶** to browse batches
- Enable **AutoGen** to auto-generate next batch
- Click **Apply These Settings to UI** to reuse parameters from a good result

### Tips
- Generate 2–4 variations (batch size) and pick the best
- Use Score to objectively compare results
- Save good results for reference
help.training_dataset:
## Dataset Builder Tutorial

### Step 1: Load or Scan
- **Load**: Enter path to existing dataset JSON → Click Load
- **Scan**: Enter audio folder path → Click Scan
  - Supported: wav, mp3, flac, ogg, opus

### Step 2: Configure
- Set **Dataset Name**
- Check **All Instrumental** if no vocals
- Set **Custom Activation Tag** (unique trigger word for your LoRA)
- Choose **Tag Position**: Prepend, Append, or Replace

### Step 3: Auto-Label
- Click **Auto-Label All** to generate captions, BPM, key, time sig
- Use **Skip Metas** to skip BPM/Key/TimeSig (faster)

### Step 4: Preview & Edit
- Use slider to browse samples
- Edit caption, lyrics, BPM, key manually
- Click **Save Changes** per sample

### Step 5: Save
- Enter save path → Click **Save Dataset**

### Step 6: Preprocess
- Set tensor output directory → Click **Preprocess**
- This encodes audio/text to tensors for training

### 📖 Documentation
- [LoRA Training Tutorial](https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5/blob/main/docs/en/LoRA_Training_Tutorial.md) — Full step-by-step guide
- [Side-Step Advanced Training](https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5/blob/main/docs/sidestep/Getting%20Started.md) — CLI-based training with advanced features
help.training_train:
## LoRA Training Tutorial

### Setup
1. Enter **Preprocessed Tensors Directory** → Click **Load Dataset**
2. Configure LoRA:
   - **Rank** (r): 64 default. Higher = more capacity
   - **Alpha**: Usually 2× rank (128)
   - **Dropout**: 0.1 for regularization

### Training
3. Set **Learning Rate** (start with 1e-4)
4. Set **Max Epochs** (500 default)
5. Click **Start Training**
6. Monitor loss curve — it should decrease over time
7. Click **Stop Training** when satisfied

### Export
8. Enter export path → Click **Export LoRA**
9. Load in Settings: set LoRA Path → Load LoRA → Enable Use LoRA

### 🚀 Try LoKr for Faster Training
LoKr has greatly improved training efficiency. What used to take an hour now only takes 5 minutes — **over 10× faster**. This is crucial for training on consumer-grade GPUs. Switch to the **Train LoKr** tab to get started.

### Tips
- Use small batch size (1) if VRAM is limited
- Gradient accumulation increases effective batch size
- Save checkpoints frequently (every 200 epochs)

### 📖 Documentation
- [LoRA Training Tutorial](https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5/blob/main/docs/en/LoRA_Training_Tutorial.md) — Full step-by-step guide
- [Side-Step Advanced Training](https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5/blob/main/docs/sidestep/Getting%20Started.md) — CLI training with corrected timesteps, LoKR, VRAM optimization
help.training_lokr:
## 🚀 LoKr Training Tutorial

LoKr (Low-rank Kronecker product) has greatly improved training efficiency. What used to take an hour with LoRA now only takes 5 minutes — **over 10× faster**. This is crucial for training on consumer-grade GPUs.

### Setup
1. Enter **Preprocessed Tensors Directory** → Click **Load Dataset**
2. Configure LoKr:
   - **Linear Dim**: 64 default (similar to LoRA rank)
   - **Linear Alpha**: 128 default (scaling factor)
   - **Weight Decompose (DoRA)**: Enabled by default for better quality

### Training
3. Set **Learning Rate** (LoKr commonly uses higher LR, start with 1e-3)
4. Set **Max Epochs** (500 default)
5. Click **Start LoKr Training**
6. Monitor loss curve — it should decrease over time
7. Click **Stop Training** when satisfied

### Export
8. Enter export path → Click **Export LoKr**
9. Load in Settings: set LoRA Path → Load LoRA → Enable Use LoRA

### LoKr vs LoRA
| | LoKr | LoRA |
|---|---|---|
| Speed | ⚡ ~10× faster | Slower |
| VRAM | Lower | Higher |
| Quality | Comparable | Baseline |
| Best for | Consumer GPUs, rapid iteration | Maximum fidelity |

### Tips
- LoKr uses Kronecker decomposition for extreme efficiency
- Enable **DoRA** (Weight Decompose) for improved quality
- Use **Tucker decomposition** for additional compression
- Higher learning rate (1e-3) often works better than LoRA's typical 1e-4
help.training_export:
## Using Your Trained LoRA

### Export
1. After training, enter export path
2. Click **Export LoRA**

### Load & Use
1. In Settings, set **LoRA Path** to your exported directory
2. Click **Load LoRA**
3. Enable **Use LoRA** checkbox
4. Generate music — your LoRA style will be applied

### Tips
- Use your **Custom Activation Tag** in captions to trigger the style
- ⚠️ LoRA is incompatible with INT8 quantization
- You can unload and switch between different LoRAs

gen.enable_normalization_info: Adjusts the final audio volume to a consistent peak level. Prevents clipping (distortion from too-loud audio) and ensures all outputs are at similar loudness. Recommended to keep enabled for consistent results.
gen.normalization_db_info: How loud the normalized audio should be. -1.0 dB = industry standard safe peak (recommended, leaves headroom). -0.1 dB = maximum loudness before clipping. Lower values (e.g. -3.0) = quieter, more headroom for further mixing/mastering.
gen.fade_in_duration_info: Gradually increases volume from silence at the start of the audio. 0 = no fade (starts at full volume). 1–3s = subtle intro. 5–10s = dramatic slow build. Useful for avoiding abrupt starts.
gen.fade_out_duration_info: Gradually decreases volume to silence at the end of the audio. 0 = no fade (may end abruptly). 2–5s = smooth ending. Useful for avoiding harsh cutoffs at the end of generated audio.
gen.latent_shift_info: Advanced: Shifts the internal audio representation before decoding. Try small negative values (e.g. -0.04) if your outputs have clipping/distortion. 0 = no shift (default). Only adjust if you're hearing audio artifacts.
gen.latent_rescale_info: Advanced: Scales the internal audio representation before decoding. Values below 1.0 (e.g. 0.91) can reduce clipping/distortion. 1.0 = no rescale (default). Only adjust if you're hearing audio artifacts despite normalization.
